sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.4 mini and nano
sources.evidence: March 17, 2026 announcement explicitly releases nano in the API. The nano column reports reasoning, tool-calling and vision benchmarks. It describes classification, extraction, ranking and simple coding tasks, but gives no numerical model size. Mini product availability and computer-use support are not transferred to nano. Reopened October 27 for the parameter re-audit: the complete launch page provides qualitative small-model positioning, prices and benchmarks, but no nominal total or active parameter count.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 nano API model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model document lists March 17 default snapshot, 400,000 context, 272,000 maximum input, 128,000 maximum output, text/image input, text output, reasoning tokens and none/low/medium/high/xhigh effort. It explicitly lists function calling, prompt caching, Chat Completions and Responses; status is deprecated. Reopened the current model documentation and its fresh October 27 Markdown cache: no total or active parameter count is published.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: March 17 entry explicitly releases gpt-5.4-nano to Chat Completions and Responses. Nano supports compaction but lacks the built-in tool-search and computer-use tools supported by mini.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: October 1, 2026 notice explicitly schedules shutdown of gpt-5.4-nano and gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17 for April 1, 2027. This date remains future at review.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived guide explicitly applies before GPT-5.6 and explains prompt caching through Transformer attention key/value projections. Combined with the exact nano caching feature, it supports a qualified broad Transformer classification, not complete block topology or counts.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses processes PDFs for vision-capable models by extracting text and page images; Chat Completions also accepts PDFs. With exact nano vision and endpoint support, PDF is an API document format rather than a separate native modality.

sources.title: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.4 nano
sources.evidence: July 31, 2026 summary specifically identifies nano and says it is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model. Training token/image/audio/video quantities are not model parameters or API modalities. It lists Union-market placement March 12, which differs from the explicit March 17 public/API launch. No neural topology or total/active parameter count is disclosed. Reopened October 27: the explicit absence of a prior-model modification/fine-tune relationship supplies no named-base count inheritance; data-volume ranges are not model size.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card
sources.evidence: The announcement-linked card includes a March 17 appendix for mini. Searching the complete extracted PDF found no nano entry or parameter disclosure for nano; neither the full model nor mini specifications are substituted for it. October 27 full-text recheck of the freshly fetched original again found no nano entry or parameter-count disclosure.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Later first-party card was checked for exact nano comparison evidence. The complete extracted document has no nano entry; full GPT-5.4 comparisons do not establish this variant size or architecture. October 27 full-text recheck of the freshly fetched original again found no nano entry or parameter-count disclosure.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Later first-party card was checked for exact nano comparison evidence. The complete extracted PDF contains NanoGPT evaluation references, but no GPT-5.4 nano entry or production parameter disclosure; NanoGPT benchmark training sizes are unrelated. October 27 full-text recheck of the freshly fetched original again found only NanoGPT benchmark mentions, not GPT-5.4 nano parameter evidence.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited service access and reserve service IP. This supports descriptive proprietary hosted-model licensing, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: Lists GPT-5.4 nano as a deprecated hosted model and separately lists gpt-oss-120b/20b as Apache-licensed open-weight models. No downloadable nano weights are offered by the checked release or model pages.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.4 nano record
sources.evidence: Catalog lead was read and used to locate exact primary benchmarks and verify its initial assertions; it is not treated as independent proof.

sources.title: Much Ado about Prompting: LLM Classification of Text Messages from Experiments
sources.publisher: Can Celebi and Stefan P. Penczynski
sources.evidence: June 16, 2026 original author-hosted paper, freshly opened October 27. Section 5.2 and Table 1 on PDF page 9 identify GPT 5.4-nano exactly and put dashes in separate Total and Active columns; the accompanying text explicitly says GPT parameter counts are undisclosed. This is the authors' original comparison, corroborating missing counts rather than providing an OpenAI disclosure or a numerical estimate.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity
sources.evidence: Original July 5, 2026 revision reopened October 27, including the exact gpt-5.4-nano row in Appendix E and the method/limitations. The row leaves parameter size and architecture unknown; the paper calibrates factual recall to effective knowledge capacity and expressly distinguishes its estimates from literal architecture. Its behavioral estimates and speculative lineage interpretations cannot supply a published total or active count.

release_date.note: Explicit public/API launch is March 17. The later training summary lists Union-market placement March 12; retain the documented public launch and record the unresolved date/scope discrepancy instead of silently treating regulatory placement as a public release.

open_weights.note: Released as a hosted API model; no downloadable nano weights identified in the checked primary release and inventory.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-service licensing classification, not an SPDX or downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit reopened the launch, exact model document, July training summary and original GPT-5.4/5.5/5.6 cards, then searched later developer disclosures and exact-model research tables. None establishes a nominal total. Celebi/Penczynski Table 1 explicitly leaves Total blank; OpenAI says nano is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model, so no named-base count is inherited. IKP effective-capacity estimates and training-data volumes are not parameter specifications.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked independently from total parameters. The exact-model sources publish no activated count, and the June Celebi/Penczynski original comparison has a separate Active column with a dash for GPT 5.4-nano. Bounded fresh searches for later activated-parameter tables found no supported nominal count. IKP behavioral capacity does not measure active parameters; no dense/MoE layout or total-equals-active assumption is made.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source inference: exact nano documentation explicitly enables prompt caching and OpenAI’s pre-GPT-5.6 technical account describes Transformer attention KV state. This is a broad Transformer-based classification only; complete block structure, dense/MoE layout and layer counts remain undisclosed.

context_window.note: Exact total context is 400,000 tokens, separately from the explicit 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output. Documentation does not establish live endpoint operation.

modalities.note: Native text/image input and text output. PDF is an API format processed into text and page images. Audio/video training sources in the public summary do not establish API audio/video support; hosted image-generation tools are not native model output.

reasoning.note: Exact nano API document lists reasoning tokens and none, low, medium, high and xhigh efforts; none as the default does not remove reasoning capability.

tool_call.note: Exact model supports function calling. Built-in computer use and tool search are explicitly unsupported; general tool support does not imply those two tools.

patch.notes: Public API launch and default snapshot are March 17, 2026. A July training summary separately lists Union-market placement March 12; this unresolved date/scope discrepancy does not override the explicit public launch. Context is 400,000 tokens, with 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output. PDF denotes API extraction into text and page images, not native PDF processing. Transformer is a qualified broad inference from exact-model prompt caching and OpenAI pre-GPT-5.6 KV documentation; detailed topology remains undisclosed. Total and active parameter counts are unpublished in the checked OpenAI sources; the June 2026 original comparison by Celebi/Penczynski explicitly leaves both blank. No prior-model size is inherited, and behavioral capacity estimates are not treated as model parameters. Deprecated October 1, 2026, with API shutdown scheduled April 1, 2027; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only re-audit retains null total and active counts with undisclosed status after reopening original OpenAI evidence and searching later disclosures. Added Celebi/Penczynski's exact-model Total/Active table, which leaves both blank, and documented rejection of IKP behavioral capacity as a size specification. OpenAI's training summary supplies no named-base lineage for count inheritance. Explicit null parameter patches and parameters_source are included; the other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
